idiom_name: public struct/class composing protocol-typed services; `internal` subsystem behind an access-controlled module
implementation_notes: Swift facades are types with a deliberately small public surface: a struct or class composes services behind protocol types and only the public declarations form the contract, while internal collaborators cannot escape the module. Protocol composition is the common shaping tool - one struct can satisfy several role protocols (file manipulation, status checking, metadata) over shared protocol extensions - and access control does the hiding that a package system does elsewhere. Foundation's FileManager is the standard-library precedent: one convenient interface over POSIX, iCloud and sandbox details.
pitfalls: Marking the facade `open` without a substitution requirement freezes its API and invites inheritance coupling; `public` plus `final` is usually enough.
Protocols the facade conforms to are part of its API: an internal protocol leaking into a public signature defeats the boundary.
Facades that own long-lived services and capture self in callbacks create retain cycles; use [weak self] or explicit teardown.
Value-type facades copy their stored services; injecting reference-type collaborators (or the singleton FileManager.default) needs an intentional choice about shared state.
